summary: Both sides are the same pattern — the whole strip as one flat colour breathing smoothly up from black to full and back with an identical envelope shape — but the port's colour is violet (peak RGB 203,0,255) where the original is hot pink/magenta (peak RGB 255,0,183), and the port's breath cycle is ~10% shorter (29.5 s vs 32.8 s).
observations: Structure: both sides are spatially uniform at every moment — a --dump at 9 times across a full cycle shows every one of the 60 pixels carrying the identical RGB triple on both sides, and an 8x8 grid re-render (--label grid8-recheck) is a flat field on both. No bands, gradient, or per-pixel structure on either side; nothing to get wrong spatially and nothing wrong.

Motion: a single global brightness breath, black -> peak -> black, no spatial travel. Normalized against its own peak the envelope is identical to two decimal places on both sides at 20 phase samples across a full cycle (0.00, 0.02, 0.09, 0.20, 0.34, 0.50, 0.65, 0.79, 0.90, 0.97, 1.00, then symmetric back down) — a smooth, symmetric, sinusoid-like fade with a brief hard-zero trough (~1.2 s at 0) at the bottom. Rise and fall are symmetric on both sides.

Period MISMATCH: measuring dark-trough midpoints over a 70 s window, original cycles every 32.78 s (troughs at 24.52 s and 57.30 s), port every 29.48 s (troughs at 22.07 s and 51.55 s). Port is ~11% faster; the phase error therefore accumulates — the two sides start roughly in step and are ~5 s apart by the second cycle.

Colour MISMATCH: both sides hold a FIXED hue for the entire cycle and scale it by brightness (green is exactly 0 at every sample on both). Original ratio B/R = 0.719 +/- 0.005 at every phase -> peak 255,0,183, hue ~317 deg, reads as hot pink / magenta. Port ratio R/B = 0.796 +/- 0.008 at every phase -> peak 203,0,255, hue ~288 deg, reads as violet / purple. A ~29 deg hue error, and since the entire pattern is that one colour it is the most visible difference between the two renders.

Peak amplitude matches: both saturate one channel to 255 at the top of the breath (orig meanBrightness max 146, port 153 — the small gap is just the hue's channel weighting, not a brightness difference).
Both sides are frame-rate invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped): identical 32.78 s / 29.48 s periods measured at 5, 10 and 20 fps. No frame-rate coupling bug on either side.
Both sides are seed-independent: --seed 7 reproduces the same trough times and same peak values as --seed 1. Nothing stochastic here.

Steady state is healthy on both: a --skip 90 --seconds 30 window shows both still hitting full peak amplitude (146 / 152) with the same cadence — no decay, no freeze, no saturation drift. No compile or runtime errors on either side in any run.

Control surface matches: the engine reports ZERO controls on both the original and the port, so --probe-controls has nothing to sweep on either side. Not a harness failure — the pattern genuinely has no dials.
feedback: Fix the hue. The pattern is one fixed colour scaled by a brightness envelope, and the port's colour is ~29 deg too far toward blue: at full brightness the original is RGB 255,0,183 (blue channel at 0.719 of red, a hot pink/magenta) while the port is RGB 203,0,255 (red at 0.796 of blue, a violet). Aim for red as the dominant channel with blue at ~72% of it, holding green at exactly 0, and keep that ratio constant across the whole fade (the original's ratio does not drift at any brightness).

Slow the breath by ~11%. The original's full black-to-peak-to-black cycle takes 32.78 s; the port's takes 29.48 s. Multiply the port's cycle rate by 0.899 (or its period by 1.112) to land on the original's cadence.

Everything else already matches and should not be touched: the flat whole-strip uniformity, the symmetric sinusoid-like fade shape, the brief full-black trough at the bottom of the cycle, the full-saturation peak, and the time-based (frame-rate-independent) clocking are all correct.
